Rationale: The source analyzes dʰapri/ɖhapri 'river bank' as Indo-Aryan dhārā 'edge, boundary' plus paray 'river', while another source labels it Korku. CDIAL 6793 is the matching edge/ridge etymon; the former automatic parent 5343 jhara 'waterfall' was only a lookalike and is rejected.

The source specifies Marathi/Hindi anjan 'ironwood' (Memecylon tinctorium). The automatic parent 12639 śōbhāñjana is Moringa pterygosperma, a different tree name; no existing Jambu node safely represents the printed ironwood comparandum, so the Indo-Aryan attribution remains an unresolved proxy.

Nihali cacav/cacāv is a close reflex of the regional Indo-Aryan cācā kin term under CDIAL 4734 *cācca-. The stored meanings 'grandchild' and, dialectally, 'wife's brother's son' show local kin-term extension; the former automatic parent 10014 mātulēya 'mother's brother's son' only acquired a cācā cross-reference and is not the correct lexical head.

The source compares Nihali bombo with Marathi bomb / bomb marɳe 'cry loudly'. CDIAL 1310 instead contains Marathi āravṇẽ/ārṇẽ 'utter its cry' and shares only the broad crying sense; it is not the printed comparandum. Because no existing Jambu node safely represents bomb, the Indo-Aryan attribution remains an unresolved proxy.

The sources compare Nihali corgi with Marathi/Hindi coli and Korku corgi 'blouse'. CDIAL 759 supplies Hindi olī 'skirt or hem or fringe', a different form reached through broad garment semantics. With no safe node for coli/corgi, the Korku–Indo-Aryan contact hypothesis remains an unresolved proxy.

The source gives only the hedged labels 'Dr., IA?' for cārumārāḍḍo 'a wild tree' and an editor separately compares Korku carmuru 'centipede'. Proto-Dravidian d2617 denotes the date palm and has no credible formal match; broad tree semantics alone cannot identify it as the source. All three printed family attributions remain questioned unresolved proxies.

The source compares bana- 'make cloth' with Hindi bunana 'weave'. CDIAL 788 contains Hindi unānā 'make bend' under avanamati 'bows'; it is a different verb selected through form overlap and a broad causative gloss. The printed Hindi comparison remains an unresolved Indo-Aryan proxy.

The source cautiously compares gayra 'much, a lot' with Hindi gahirā 'deep'. CDIAL 4502 is ghr̥tapūra, a sweetmeat name, and its Hindi gʰīūrā denotes a cucumber; neither is the printed adjective. The possible Indo-Aryan comparison remains unresolved.

The source only marks nīl 'wild cow' as possibly Hindi. CDIAL 1593 is *illi 'kite', and the Hindi īl 'wild animal' descendant is neither a cow term nor an identified source form. A broad wild-animal gloss is insufficient, so the Indo-Aryan label remains an unresolved proxy.

The source compares salāy 'sal tree' with Marathi śāla 'Shorea robusta'. CDIAL 12369 is śāka 'teak' and its Marathi sāylā descendant is also glossed 'teak tree'; this is a different botanical name. With no safe sal-tree node, the Indo-Aryan comparison remains an unresolved proxy.

The source compares bʰānḍa-kunḍa 'vessels' with Hindi bhāṇḍa 'pot'. CDIAL 9395 is bharaṇa 'bearing' and the matched Hindi bharnā is a sugarcane-juice vessel; it is not bhāṇḍa. The transparent Hindi vessel component remains an unresolved Indo-Aryan proxy.

The source compares ḍecki 'water-storage vessel' with Korku ɖhecki 'small metal pot' while giving only a general Indo-Aryan label. CDIAL 5596 *ḍhēṅka denotes a weight or lever, and its ḍhẽki water-lifting reflex is not a vessel. The Korku–Indo-Aryan attribution remains an unresolved proxy.

The source compares arado with Marathi arɖa/araɖa 'cry loudly'. CDIAL 1302 āraṭati 'shrieks' contains Marathi āraḍṇẽ/araḍṇẽ 'cry out, bellow' and is the exact lexical head; the former automatic parent 8952 prārabdhi 'killing' was selected through the hunting context and an unrelated Marathi pārad 'hunting'.

The source explicitly cites CDIAL 9330 *bhakkha and its Sinhala baka/bakkā 'big' forms for bʰāgā pasārā 'broad'. The former automatic parent 861 *avasāra 'moving aside' matched only a descendant glossed 'wide' and ignored the cited head.

The source compares nindo 'sleep' with dialectal Marathi nind and Marathi nidā. CDIAL 7200 nidrā 'sleep' is the appropriate nominal head and includes nind-type descendants; the former parent 7382 niryāti 'goes out, dies' contains secondary sleep senses but is not the printed comparison.

The note attached to bʰum cippoka cites only Indo-Aryan wandering roots (CDIAL 9648 and possibly 9561), presumably for the bʰum component. The automatic parent 9188a bahutara 'more, many' was inferred from the English gloss 'more than one' and is absent from the source evidence. The printed Indo-Aryan component hypothesis remains an unresolved proxy.

For bʰagel hela 'all big people', the source explicitly cites CDIAL 9330 *bhakkha and its Sinhala baka/bakkā 'big' forms. The former automatic parent 11225 vaḍra 'big' matched the meaning but ignored the cited etymon.
